subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` categorically fail closed on legacy ownerless session rows, matching delete semantics, or must OpenClaw provide a doctor migration or explicit operator adoption path first?
rationale: The choice controls both cross-plugin isolation and upgrade compatibility for persisted rows created before plugin ownership metadata existed; tests cannot establish the intended product and security policy.

options.title: Keep exact-owner fail closed
options.body: Reject ownerless rows for plugin runtimes and document operator or non-plugin management as the supported recovery path.

options.title: Add ownership migration
options.body: Require doctor or an explicit operator adoption workflow to resolve legacy rows before exact-owner enforcement lands.

recommendation.title: Keep exact-owner fail closed
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows for plugin runtimes and document operator or non-plugin management as the supported recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to the central `sessions.patch` handler and current session mutation behavior, making them the strongest available routing candidate for the boundary decision.
